top.line: An ABP governs; attestation lets others verify
top.para: Checking someone's summary of how ruv.sgit fits an assurance layer: an ABP does not enforce by itself. It names the level that keeps each rule: prompt, hooks, or a recommended third-party system such as Ruflo's policy engine, whose receipts an sgit vault keeps. Attestation signs what was assured so third parties can verify.

in-short.line: Govern, enforce at three levels, record, attest
in-short.para: The summary was nearly right; 'enforces' needed precision. ABP governs and names the enforcer. Rules are kept in the prompt, by hooks, or by a third-party blocker. Receipts come from the enforcer. Attestation makes it verifiable outside.

summary.line: A summary checked before it was shared
summary.para: Someone working on agent assurance described ABP as governing and enforcing, with their layer attesting so a third party can verify. Dinis found it almost right, except the word enforces.

abp.line: A policy that names its enforcer
abp.para: An ABP states each role's reach, mandate and rules, and what keeps each rule; a rule only the agent keeps is a hope, one something else keeps is a control. It governs, and names the enforcer.

levels.line: Prompt, hooks, or a third-party system that blocks
levels.para: Rules can be kept in the prompt (hope), by deterministic hooks on the agent's machine, or by a third-party system out of the agent's reach, the recommended level. In ruv.sgit, Ruflo's policy engine in enforce mode is that system, covering the tools that pass through it.

receipt.line: Mandate, receipt and memory live in different places
receipt.para: The mandate is the ABP; the receipt is written by the enforcer, Ruflo's policy engine; the memory, with the receipts, is in an sgit vault. That defines what can be attested.

missing.line: Without attestation, outsiders take the operator's word
missing.para: Customers, auditors and insurers today must trust the operator's logs. Attestation signs the policy version, each rule's level, the receipts and the record's hash, and should say which rules were controls and which were only hopes.

flow.line: One action, from tool call to outside check
flow.para: Agent proposes; a hook warns; the policy engine decides and writes a receipt; the vault keeps it; attestation signs; a verifier checks.

layers.para: ABP governs and names how rules are kept; Ruflo enforces and receipts; sgit records; attestation signs. A natural early integration, because the ABP already marks controls and hopes.

limits.para: The attestation layer is its makers' design. Three levels simplify five. Enforce mode covers only the tools passing through it. Signing proves integrity, not that the policy is good.

sources.para: Dinis's note of 19 October 2026, answering a summary described but not quoted, with ruv.sgit.ai and the newsroom's articles on policies and hooks.
